# Veterans Healing Farm

> Veterans Healing Farm (VHF) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit farm in Mills River, North Carolina, founded in 2013 by John and Nicole Mahshie. It supports the mental, emotional, and physical well-being of veterans and their families in Western North Carolina through farm-based therapy, community, and purpose. Its vision is an end to the veteran suicide crisis.

- Address: 138 Kimzey Road, Mills River, NC 28759
- Phone: (828) 595-6111
- Area served: mostly Henderson, Buncombe, and Transylvania counties in North Carolina, with some veterans coming from Tennessee, South Carolina, Georgia, and Virginia
- Email: veteranshealingfarm@gmail.com
- Farm hours: Tuesday to Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm. Saturday hours vary, so call ahead. Closed Sunday and Monday.
- Everything the farm grows is donated to veterans and local organizations, including the Charles George VA Medical Center and the Veterans Restoration Quarters in Asheville.
- In crisis? The Veterans Crisis Line is free and open 24/7: call 988 and press 1, or text 838255.

## Programs

- [Programs](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/programs): Agritherapy (vegetable and flower gardens, beekeeping, medicinal herbs), Clay & Camaraderie pottery with a resident potter, therapeutic workshops, and community events.
- [Event calendar](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/events): Upcoming workshops, volunteer groups, and gatherings, with registration.
- [Resources](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/resources): Free VA apps for PTSD, sleep, stress, anger, relationships, and alcohol use.

## Get involved

- [Volunteer](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/volunteer): You don't have to be a veteran. No experience or set schedule needed. Join the Garden Group (vegetables and flowers), the Medicinal Herb Squad, the Bee Squad, or a volunteer committee.
- [Donate](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/donate): Online giving, an Amazon wish list, and other ways to support the farm.
- [Contact](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/contact): Directions, hours, and how to reach the farm.
- [FAQ](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/faq): Who can come, cost, hours, tours, volunteering, giving, and crisis help, answered briefly.

## For funders and grantmakers

- Mission focus: veteran mental health and suicide prevention. Programs center on brain health, healing through hands-on work, and peer connection.
- 2026 results (2026 Year-End Report): 96 therapeutic workshops serving 852 participants, including pottery, beekeeping, blacksmithing, acupuncture, equine programs, medicinal herbs, music, art, dog training, nutrition, outdoor recreation, and Mental Health First Aid.
- Giving back: in 2026 the farm grew and donated 2,683 lbs of fresh produce and more than 500 flower bouquets, grew 46 medicinal plants, produced 2,235 herbal products, and harvested 15 gallons of honey, all at no cost to veterans. Since it began, the farm has grown and donated nearly 80,000 lbs of produce.
- No cost to veterans: everything the farm provided in 2026 was free to veterans and their families.
- Growth in 2026: a new pottery studio and an outdoor performance and teaching stage.
- A regional gathering place: in 2026 the farm hosted a U.S. Army Change of Command ceremony, Quilts of Valor presentations, an Easter egg hunt for more than 80 children, and the Governor's Institute WNC Working Group with more than 40 veteran organizations. The 2nd Annual Women Warriors' Leadership Luncheon drew more than 200 attendees. The farm presented its work at the Governor's Institute in Raleigh and at the National Endowment for the Arts national meeting in Asheville.
- Volunteer-powered: 411 volunteers in 2026 alongside a very small staff, many of them veterans, so most grants and donations go straight into the farm and its programs.
- Accountability: registered 501(c)(3) with public IRS Form 990s and a North Carolina charitable solicitation license. Online gifts, one time or monthly, are made through PayPal. Checks payable to Veterans Healing Farm can be mailed to the farm, and gifts by will or estate plan are welcome. Active SAM.gov registration. EIN 46-5689396.
- Community partners who receive the farm's produce and flowers include the Charles George VA Medical Center, the Storehouse, SafeLight Women's Shelter / Dandelion Café, IAM Food Pantry, the Rescue Mission, Carolina Reserve of Laurel Park and Hendersonville, and The Landing.
- [2025 Year-End Report (PDF)](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/s/VHF_Impact-Report-2025_Draft2.pdf): the most recent full report posted as a PDF (the 2026 figures above come from the 2026 Year-End Report).
- Sponsorship and partnership: [Sponsors](https://www.veteranshealingfarm.org/sponsors), or email veteranshealingfarm@gmail.com
